title: Hair Whorl: What It Is and What Research Shows
seo_title: Hair Whorl: Normal Patterns, Genetics & Hair Growth | FullyVital
seo_description: What a hair whorl is, which whorl patterns are normal, what research says about genetics, and why there is no evidence that it affects hair growth.
notes: Citation style v2: 3 studies, each cited once, all in the second half; Key Takeaways and FAQ carry no links.
Old post (1,760 words, 0 study links) claimed the whorl is 'a key to hair growth'. No study supports that, so the title and claims were removed.
flags: The closing FullyVital product box (unchanged, sitewide) says products 'Promote Hair Regrowth'. Left for you, as with boron.

The Samlaska 1989 abstract says abnormal or absent whorls have been associated with abnormal brain development. The article reports it neutrally with the 'normal development' cases and without alarm. Check your comfort with that line on a parent-facing page.
Styling tips are general advice, not from the abstracts. Evidence is thin; you may prefer to hold or merge it.
